s: WWII fortress plan guarding the Gotthard passes
w: From the 1880s, Switzerland built a defensive plan around the fortress complexes of St Gotthard, St Maurice and Sargans, expanded in the Second World War against a feared German invasion, aiming to deny an aggressor the Alpine passes and rail tunnels running north-south through this region.
_facts: Swiss defensive plan developed from the 1880s, expanded early in WWII against a feared German invasion
Centred on the fortress complexes of St Maurice, St Gotthard and Sargans
Aimed to deny an invader passage over or through the Alps by controlling major passes and rail tunnels
Defended the alpine crossings between Germany and Italy, outside Switzerland's industrialised heartland

s: 3,417m high point east of the Susten Pass
w: Also called Rot Stock, the Fleckistock reaches 3,417m above Wassen in the canton of Uri, the high point of a chain running east from the Sustenjoch pass. Glaciers cover its eastern flanks, and climbers usually start out from the Voralp hut, at 2,126m, owned by the Swiss Alpine Club.
_facts: 3,417m mountain of the Urner Alps overlooking Wassen, also called Rot Stock
Highest summit of the group lying east of the Sustenjoch pass (2,656m)
Glaciers Rutifirn and Kartigelfirn cover its eastern flanks
Normal route climbs from the Voralp hut (2,126m), owned by the Swiss Alpine Club

w: The Goscheneralpsee reservoir, in the municipality of Goschenen, holds 76 million cubic metres of water across a surface of 1.32 square kilometres, ringed by the peaks of the Urner Alps at the head of a valley the Gotthard rail line passes through far below.
_facts: Reservoir in the municipality of Goschenen, canton of Uri
Volume of 76 million cubic metres
Surface area of 1.32 square kilometres

s: Reservoir dam (1947) at the Gotthard Pass
w: Lago di Lucendro sits right at the St Gotthard Pass, in the municipality of Airolo, held back by a dam completed in 1947 and standing 73 metres high - one of a string of hydroelectric reservoirs engineered into the high Gotthard landscape in the years after the war.
_facts: Reservoir at the St Gotthard Pass, municipality of Airolo, canton of Ticino
Dam 73 metres high, completed in 1947

s: 3,096m high point of the Glarus Alps
w: Also known as Schattig Wichel, Piz Giuv straddles the border of Uri and Graubunden at 3,096m, the highest point of the Glarus Alps west of the Oberalpstock. Its summit sits where three valleys meet - the Fellital and Etzlital to the north, the Val Giuv to the south - with the slightly lower Piz Nair just to its east.
_facts: 3,096m mountain of the Glarus Alps on the Uri-Graubunden border, also called Schattig Wichel
Highest mountain of the Glarus Alps lying west of the Oberalpstock
Summit sits between the Fellital and Etzlital valleys (north) and Val Giuv (south)
Piz Nair, slightly lower, lies on its east side

w: Pizzo Lucendro rises 2,963m on the border between Uri and Ticino, looking straight down on both the St Gotthard Pass and the reservoir that shares its name. The Lepontine Alps summit is a short, obvious target for anyone already standing at the pass below.
_facts: 2,963m mountain of the Lepontine Alps on the Uri-Ticino border
Overlooks the St Gotthard Pass and Lago di Lucendro on its east side

s: Glacier-ringed peak near the Susten Pass
w: The Stucklistock overlooks the Meiental valley in the canton of Uri, a few kilometres southeast of the Susten Pass. Glaciers ring the mountain, the largest of them the Rutifirn, spilling down its eastern flank into the valley below.
_facts: Mountain of the Urner Alps overlooking the Meiental valley, canton of Uri
Lies a few kilometres southeast of the Susten Pass
Surrounded by glaciers, the largest named Rutifirn, on its east flank

s: 1947 dam by engineer Fritz Gigax, Gotthard Pass
w: Lago della Sella, a reservoir near the St Gotthard Pass in Ticino, is held by a 36-metre gravity dam completed in 1947. It was designed and built under the direction of Swiss engineer Fritz Gigax, one of several high-altitude dams engineered into the Gotthard massif that same year.
_facts: Reservoir near the St Gotthard Pass, canton of Ticino
Gravity dam 36 metres high, completed in 1947
Built under the direction of Swiss engineer Fritz Gigax

s: High point above Val Maighels and Lake Curnera
w: Piz Ravetsch is the high point of the ridge separating the Val Maighels from the valley holding Lake Curnera, in Graubunden near the Ticino border. The Glatscher da Maighels, a sizeable glacier, still covers much of its western flank, feeding the valley's streams below.
_facts: Mountain of the Lepontine Alps in Graubunden, near the Ticino border
Highest summit of the range separating Val Maighels from the valley of Lake Curnera
Glacier Glatscher da Maighels covers its western flank

s: Massif where four major European rivers rise
w: Called the water tower of Europe, the Gotthard Massif gives rise to three major rivers - the Reuss, the Rhine and the Ticino - with the Rhone rising just north of it near the Furka Pass. A trekking route, the Vier-Quellen-Weg or Four Springs Trail, crosses the massif to link all four sources.
_facts: Mountain range at the border of Valais, Ticino, Uri and Graubunden, called the water tower of Europe
Source of the Reuss, Rhine and Ticino rivers; the Rhone rises just north of the massif near the Furka Pass
The Gotthard Pass, at its heart, is the main north-south route through the range
The Vier-Quellen-Weg (Four Springs Trail) crosses the massif linking all four river sources

s: 1948 west ridge, and a 2009 suspension bridge
w: Rock climbers have tackled the Salbitschijen's ridges since 1935; the harder west ridge, once thought unclimbable, fell only in 1948. In 2009 a high suspension bridge, the Salbitbrucke, was strung across its southern flank, letting hikers cross between two huts, though most still rope up for the exposed approach.
_facts: Mountain of the Urner Alps overlooking Goschenen, known for rock climbing
Southern ridges first climbed in 1935; the west ridge, once thought inaccessible, first climbed 1948
In 2009 a high suspension bridge, the Salbitbrucke, was installed on its southern flank
Bridge links the Salbithutte and Voralphutte huts; via ferrata gear is used on the exposed path

s: Natural lake dammed since 1918 to power the rail line
w: Lago Ritom, a natural lake in Ticino's Piora valley, has helped power the Gotthard rail line since the Swiss Federal Railways first dammed it in 1918 to generate hydroelectricity; the dam was raised a further 23 metres in 1950 to expand the supply for the line running far below.
_facts: Natural lake in the Piora valley, canton of Ticino
Used as a reservoir by the Swiss Federal Railways to power the Gotthard line
First dam built in 1918; raised by 23 metres in 1950
